quote: The roofs are shining from the rain, / The sparrows twitter as they fly, / And with a windy April grace / The little clouds go by. / Yet the back-yards are bare and brown / With only one unchanging tree— / I could not be so sure of Spring / Save that it sings in me.
source: Sara Teasdale, April, the whole poem, Rivers to the Sea (Macmillan, 1915)

evidence.where: Two Internet Archive scans of the Macmillan 1915 first edition, the Cornell copy and the Google scanned copy, read as OCR text this run, and Project Gutenberg ebook 596 as a clean transcription; the three agree
evidence.edition: Rivers to the Sea (New York: The Macmillan Company, 1915)
evidence.locator: April, both quatrains, the complete eight line poem

reason: Both 1915 scans carry the dash after tree and the comma after fly, and Gutenberg 596 agrees; the proposal had only Gutenberg behind it, so the evidence here is the first edition itself. The printed page sets the opening word in small capitals, a convention used for every poem in the book, and it is rendered The. Teasdale is not shipped, not banned, at zero of three.
